speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing agitation and have noticed a yellowish tint to your skin and eyes. To help me assess this, have you been consuming alcohol or taking any new medications or supplements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and new-onset jaundice, I need to check for viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_A_IgM, Hepatitis_B_surface_antigen, Hepatitis_C_antibody.

text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 16.3 g/dL, Hematocrit: 47%, Leukocyte Count: 9,750/mm3, Neutrophils: 58%, Bands: 2%, Eosinophils: 1%, Basophils: 0%, Lymphocytes: 24%, Monocytes: 2%, Platelet Count: 365,000/mm3, Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: Those labs indicate severe acute liver failure with significant coagulopathy and hyperbilirubinemia. Given your high-risk sexual history, I must rule out Hepatitis E or other viral causes, so I need to know: have you experienced any recent fever, nausea, or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe acute liver failure and high-risk sexual history, I need to confirm if you have had any recent unprotected anal intercourse. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_E_IgM

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Hepatitis E result and the specific lab pattern of very high bilirubin with only moderately elevated transaminases, along with a history of ecstasy use, strongly suggest acetaminophen toxicity, possibly from undisclosed ingestion. REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: The toxic acetaminophen level confirms acute acetaminophen-induced liver failure. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acetaminophen toxicity
